label: prf:confinement-phase-stratification
title: Proof of confinement phase stratification
html:
Proof. Proof of confinement phase stratification

Proof. Claim (1)—Openness. Slater-strict feasibility of an SDP is preserved under small perturbations of the defining data (Boyd–Vandenberghe Lemma 5.4.1). If \Phi_0 \succ 0 is strictly feasible at q_0, then for every q in a neighbourhood of q_0, the same \Phi_0 remains strictly feasible due to the continuity of the SDP constraint matrices in q. Hence, \Omega(P) is a union of open neighbourhoods and is therefore open.

Claim (2)—Stratification. The complement \mathcal{G} \setminus \Omega(P) is defined by the vanishing of a finite product of principal-minor determinants of the Gram matrix \mathrm{G}(q). Each determinant is a polynomial in q with finitely many real zeros in \mathcal{G}. The union of these zero sets forms a real-algebraic stratification. Generic strata have codimension 1 (single-minor vanishing), while lower strata appear at simultaneous vanishings.

Claim (3)—Local constancy. On each component \Omega_\alpha, the active support \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) is determined by the sign pattern of the complementary-slackness dual variables u_\lambda^*(q). By the continuity of the SDP optimiser in q (generic uniqueness from Slater strictness, Boyd–Vandenberghe §5.5.3) and the integer-valuedness of |\mathcal{S}^*|, the set \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) cannot change within \Omega_\alpha. Any change requires some u_\lambda^* to pass through zero, which precisely defines the phase-boundary condition. Continuity of \sigma_F follows directly from the continuity of the SDP optimal value under Slater regularity.

Claim (4)—Scope. The proofs of prop:level-sufficiency (Markov-inclusion + active-support preservation) and prop:shell-closure-stability (SDP-relaxation monotonicity + multi-block tightness) both assume the active support is well-defined and locally constant (i.e., q \in \Omega_\alpha). If any of the three properties in Claim (3) fails on \partial\Omega(P), it invalidates the corresponding proof. Therefore, the scope is strictly confined to the open stratum.

Claim (5)—Phase transitions. A boundary crossing at q_0 represents either a Slater-loss event (primal strict PSD feasibility breaks \to deconfinement) or an active-support transition (some u_\lambda^* passes through zero \to regime switch with \mu-jump). Both correspond precisely to the discrete-regime-switch phenomenology documented in prop:parity-regime-selection and the deconfinement golden threshold. \square

Corollary (phase-scoped applicability). We implicitly restrict the scope of any theorem, proposition, or definition in the confinement framework referencing def:confined-particle, def:confinement-category, prop:confinement-sdp, prop:level-sufficiency, def:electron-shell, def:dressed-particle, or prop:shell-closure-stability to "for all q \in \Omega_\alpha(P), some fixed confinement phase of P". Statements that must hold across phase boundaries (e.g., phase-transition signatures, critical exponents, scaling laws) require explicit boundary analysis; within-phase theorems do not cover them.
